room.control_mode.full_control_info: RoomMind has full control over your climate devices. An external temperature sensor provides the actual room temperature, enabling proportional setpoint calculation. The device setpoint is dynamically adjusted based on MPC power output. The thermal model (EKF) learns your room's behavior for optimal comfort and energy efficiency.
room.control_mode.managed_info: RoomMind sets the target temperature on your device (from schedule, override, or vacation settings), but the device self-regulates using its own internal sensor. No proportional boost, no thermal model learning, and no MPC optimization. For more precise control, assign an external temperature sensor in the Devices section.
room.climate_control_hint: When disabled, RoomMind stops controlling devices in this room. They keep their current settings and may continue heating or cooling on their own. RoomMind will not turn them off.
room.outdoor_hint: Disables climate control, mold detection, and model training. Sensor monitoring continues.

hero.mpc_learning_paused.outdoor_unavail: RoomMind needs an outdoor temperature to learn this room's thermal model. The configured outdoor sensor is unavailable and no weather entity is set as a fallback. Configure either in Settings.
hero.compressor_protection_info: This room shares an outdoor compressor with other rooms. To prevent short-cycling, the shared compressor group enforces a minimum run time and a minimum off time before this device is allowed to switch again.

schedule.help_temps_title: How is the target temperature determined?
schedule.help_temps: The target temperature follows this priority chain:
schedule.help_temps_1: Manual override – A temporary boost/eco/custom override always takes highest priority.
schedule.help_temps_2: Block temperature – If the active schedule block has a temperature value in its data, that value is used.
schedule.help_temps_3: Comfort temperature – If the schedule is "on" but the block has no temperature, the comfort fallback temperature below is used.
schedule.help_temps_4: Eco temperature – When the schedule is "off" (outside all time blocks), the eco temperature is used.
schedule.help_block: You can set a specific temperature for each time block by adding a temperature value in the schedule's YAML configuration:
schedule.help_block_note: If a block has no temperature data, the comfort fallback temperature is used instead.
schedule.help_split: For auto-mode rooms, you can set separate heating and cooling targets per time block using heat_temperature and cool_temperature:
schedule.help_split_note: If only one is set, the other falls back to the room's comfort temperature. These keys take priority over temperature when present.
schedule.help_multi: You can add multiple schedules and switch between them using a selector entity. This can be an input_boolean (toggles between schedule 1 and 2) or an input_number (selects by number). Without a selector entity, only the first schedule is used.
schedule.comfort_hint_auto: Comfort: target when schedule is on. Eco: target when schedule is off. Rows set the target for heating and cooling.
schedule.comfort_hint: Used when schedule is "on" but no temperature is set in the block
devices.no_climate: No climate entities found in this area.
devices.no_temp_sensors: No temperature sensors found in this area.
devices.no_humidity_sensors: No humidity sensors found in this area.
devices.no_occupancy_sensors: No occupancy sensors found in this area
devices.occupancy_sensor_hint: Improves thermal model accuracy by tracking room occupancy
devices.no_window_sensors: No window/door sensors found in this area.
devices.wall_factor_hint: How cold the room's coldest wall spot is: used to estimate humidity where mold forms. Lower = colder wall = higher risk.
devices.wall_measure_hint: Calibrate with a measurement: on a cold day, measure the moldy spot with an infrared thermometer (surface mode).
devices.wall_measure_invalid: Measurement not usable: needs at least 5 °C between room and outdoor and a result between 0.50 and 0.95.
devices.heating_system_type_info: After heating stops, radiators and especially underfloor systems continue to release stored heat. RoomMind accounts for this residual heat to avoid overshooting and improve model accuracy. Underfloor rooms also get longer minimum run times.
devices.underfloor_delay_hint: Underfloor heating has long restart times. A window-open delay of at least 5 minutes is recommended to avoid unnecessary shutoffs.
devices.heating_system_type_boost_hint: Tip: If the heating system has changed, you can accelerate re-learning under Settings.
devices.idle_action_low_hint: Lowers the setpoint to the device minimum instead of sending off. Prevents TRVs that hibernate in off mode from losing later commands.
devices.fan_only_require_presence: Only when tracked people are home
devices.fan_only_season_hint: Season filters require Home Assistant's Season integration, which provides sensor.season. If it is unavailable, fan-only stays off.
devices.setpoint_mode_hint: Direct sends the actual room target to the device — best for thermostats and space heaters that regulate themselves. Proportional sends a boosted setpoint toward the device max_temp — best for radiator valves (TRVs).
devices.valve_protection_exclude_hint: This entity will not be cycled by valve protection (e.g. virtual boiler entities)
devices.info.types_body: Thermostat means a radiator thermostat / TRV. Climate Device means an AC, heat pump, or other climate entity used for cooling or forced-air heating. Both are Home Assistant climate entities; the distinction is how RoomMind controls them.
devices.info.control_body: Setpoint mode only applies to thermostats in Full Control rooms with an external temperature sensor. Use Proportional when RoomMind should drive heating output by sending boosted setpoints. Use Direct when the device should regulate itself around the real target temperature.
devices.info.modes_body: When idle only applies to Climate Devices. Turn off powers the device down. Fan only keeps airflow without heating or cooling. Setback keeps the current mode active but moves the target 2°C away from the room target. This setback offset is currently fixed. For Thermostats, Low keeps the TRV active at its minimum setpoint instead of off, useful for battery-powered Zigbee TRVs that sleep when set to off.
devices.info.heat_source_body: This appears only when a room has both a thermostat/TRV and a Climate Device plus an external temperature sensor. RoomMind can then choose which source should handle heating based on temperature gap and outdoor conditions.
covers.auto_control_hint: RoomMind closes blinds when solar gain is predicted to overheat the room.
covers.deploy_threshold_hint: Close blinds when predicted temperature exceeds target by this amount.
covers.min_position_hint: Blinds will never close further than this (0 = fully closed allowed).
covers.override_minutes_hint: How long to pause automatic control after manual cover movement. Set to 0 for no pause.
covers.no_covers_in_area: No cover entities found in this area.
covers.night_close_hint: Automatically close covers at sunset and open at sunrise.
covers.schedule_section_hint: Define time windows for cover control using HA schedule helpers. In Force position mode the schedule's position overrides solar/thermal logic. In Allow solar protection mode RoomMind decides the position within the active window.
covers.schedule_position_hint: Cover position when this schedule is active (0% = fully closed, 100% = fully open).
covers.schedule_selector_hint: Choose which schedule is active. input_boolean: off=#1, on=#2. input_number: value selects schedule number.
covers.schedule_selector_warning: Multiple schedules configured but no selector set. Only the first schedule will be used.
covers.night_position_hint: Cover position when night close is active (0% = fully closed). Covers with an individual min. position will never go below that.
covers.night_close_elevation_hint: How far below or above the horizon the sun must be. 0° = exactly at sunset/sunrise. Negative = darker (e.g. -6° = dusk, when it's noticeably dark). Positive = still bright (e.g. 5° = sun still visible above horizon).
covers.night_close_offset_hint: Additional shift relative to the sun position threshold. Positive = close later (e.g. +20 = 20 min after threshold is reached), negative = close earlier.
covers.outdoor_min_temp_hint: Don't close covers for solar protection below this outdoor temperature. Solar heat gain is welcome when it's cold.
covers.per_cover_hint: Set the compass direction each cover faces and optional individual minimum positions.
covers.per_cover_min_position_hint: Individual minimum position per cover. Covers will never close further than this. Useful when blinds are physically fully closed at a position > 0%.
covers.snap_deploy_hint: Close covers directly to the minimum position instead of gradually closing. Recommended for triple-pane windows where intermediate positions can cause thermal stress.
covers.info.selection_body: Select covers/blinds from this area or add entities from other areas. RoomMind tracks their position and can control them automatically.
covers.info.schedule_body: Use HA schedule helpers to define times when covers should close (e.g. privacy in the evening). The schedule's position attribute determines how far they close. Schedules override all other automatic logic.
covers.info.solar_body: When automatic control is enabled, RoomMind predicts whether solar radiation will overheat the room and closes blinds preventively. It uses learned thermal data when available, otherwise a conservative default. The deploy threshold controls how much predicted overshoot is needed before blinds close.
covers.info.night_body: Closes covers at sunset and opens them at sunrise. You can set a custom night position (e.g. 10% = almost closed but not fully).
covers.info.override_body: If you manually move a cover, RoomMind detects this and pauses automatic control for the configured duration. This prevents fighting with the user.
covers.info.priority_body: Manual override > Schedule > Night close > Solar/thermal control. Higher priority rules always win. When no rule applies, covers stay open.
covers.info.entities_body: RoomMind creates two entities per room for external use: switch.roommind_{area}_cover_auto (enable/disable automatic cover control — usable in automations or dashboards) and binary_sensor.roommind_{area}_cover_paused (on when manual override is active, e.g. after manually moving a cover).
covers.orientation_hint: Set the compass direction each cover faces. RoomMind uses this to skip solar deployment when the sun is not shining on that side of the building.
settings.climate_control_hint: When disabled, RoomMind continues to monitor all sensors and train the model, but sends no commands to your heating or cooling devices. Your devices keep their current mode and setpoint and may continue heating or cooling on their own. RoomMind will not turn them off.
settings.learning_hint: When paused, RoomMind stops collecting new measurement data and training the thermal model. Existing model data is preserved.
settings.smart_control_hint: Configure outdoor temperature limits for heating and cooling.
settings.outdoor_cooling_min_hint: AC stays off when outdoor temperature is below this value
settings.outdoor_heating_max_hint: Heating stays off when outdoor temperature exceeds this value
settings.comfort_weight_hint: Balances temperature precision against energy use. Comfort reacts earlier and stays closer to target. Efficiency allows more drift to reduce heating/cooling runtime.
settings.weather_entity_hint: Optional: enables predictive outdoor temperature planning, and acts as a fallback when the outdoor sensor is unavailable
settings.outdoor_unavailable_notify: Notify when outdoor temperature is unavailable
settings.outdoor_unavailable_notify_hint: Show a Home Assistant notification when neither the outdoor sensor nor the weather entity has reported a temperature for 30 minutes. While this is the case, RoomMind pauses thermal model learning to avoid corruption.
settings.prediction_enabled_hint: Show predicted temperature trend in analytics charts. Disable if you experience slow performance.
vacation.title: Vacation Mode
vacation.hint: Sets all rooms to a setback temperature until the end date.
energy_subtitle: Measured AC demand and learned 3-hour forecast
analytics.info.accuracy_idle: How precisely the model predicts temperature when neither heating nor cooling is active. A lower value means the model understands your room's natural heat loss well. This is the first value to improve because idle data is collected continuously.
analytics.info.accuracy_heating: How precisely the model predicts temperature during active heating. This value stays high initially because the model needs real heating cycles to learn from. Once your heating has run a few times, this value will drop and MPC control becomes available.
analytics.info.confidence: Overall model readiness for intelligent MPC control, combining two factors: data quantity (how many idle and active-mode samples have been collected) and prediction accuracy (how precise the temperature forecasts are). Confidence starts at 0% and rises as the model collects data and learns. Around 50% means enough idle data but still waiting for heating/cooling cycles. Above 80% means the model has enough data and accurate predictions — MPC control becomes available. 100% is the theoretical maximum when predictions are as accurate as physically possible.
analytics.info.time_constant: How long it takes your room to naturally cool down halfway toward the outdoor temperature when heating is off. A longer time constant means better insulation — the room holds warmth longer. A short time constant means the room cools quickly. The model learns this by observing temperature drops during idle periods.
analytics.info.heating_rate: How strongly your heating affects the room temperature. A higher value means your heating system warms the room faster relative to its thermal mass. The model learns this by observing how quickly the temperature rises during active heating, and uses it to predict how long heating needs to run.
analytics.info.cooling_rate: How strongly your AC affects the room temperature. A higher value means the AC cools the room faster relative to its thermal mass. The model learns this by observing how quickly the temperature drops during active cooling, and uses it to predict how long the AC needs to run.
analytics.info.solar_gain: The estimated effect of solar radiation through windows on room temperature. The model learns this by observing how the room warms during sunny periods when heating is off. Rooms with large south-facing windows will have higher values. The model uses this to reduce heating when solar gain is expected.
analytics.info.occupancy_gain: The estimated heat contribution from occupancy (people, pets, computers) while the room is occupied. The model learns this by observing temperature changes when the configured occupancy sensors are active. Separating this from solar gain prevents body heat from being misattributed to sunlight. Only shown when at least one occupancy sensor is configured for this room.
analytics.info.residual_afterglow: How much heat your radiators keep giving off after a heating run, learned by watching how far the room still warms after each run: × is the multiple of the standard radiator profile, min how long the stored heat takes to fade. Runs disturbed by an open window, an AC heating or the boiler are skipped. It changes heating only in rooms where “Use the learned afterglow” is on (“Schedule & Temperatures” section): there radiators stop earlier and needless preheating is skipped. Shown for radiator rooms once at least one run was learned.
analytics.info.data_sources: Number of measurement samples used for model training.
analytics.info.data_points: Total number of observations the model has been trained on. More data points generally lead to better predictions. The model collects a new data point roughly every 3 minutes while RoomMind is running.
analytics.no_data: No data yet — model is learning
settings.reset_hint: Clear learned thermal model data and history. The model will start learning from scratch.
settings.reset_all_hint: Clear thermal data and history for all rooms at once.
settings.reset_all_confirm: Clear all learned thermal data and history for ALL rooms? All models will start learning from scratch.
settings.reset_room_hint: Select a room to clear its thermal data and history.
settings.reset_room_confirm: Clear all learned thermal data and history for this room? The model will start learning from scratch.
settings.boost_hint: The thermal model learns your room's heating and cooling behavior over time. After major changes (new radiator, AC, insulation, furniture), the model may be inaccurate. This increases the model's uncertainty so it adapts faster to new conditions.
analytics.chart_info_body:
**Lines:** The solid line is the measured room temperature, the green dashed line the target in force. Right of the now line: target and prediction (dotted) for the next 3 hours.

**Target range:** The figures above count the pale green band as on target: from {tolerance} below the heating target up to {tolerance} above the cooling target (heat only: everything from the heating side up, cool only: everything from the cooling side down). Below it is tinted pale blue (too cold), above it pale red (too warm).

**Strip and areas:** The strip along the bottom shows when the room heated (orange) or cooled (blue), a gray area an open window.

**Below:** Outdoor temperature; humidity with a green band for 40–60 % (line yellow at 30–40 and 60–70 %, red beyond; too dry irritates the airways, too humid favors mold on cold walls).
presence.title: Presence Detection
presence.hint: Uses eco temperature when nobody is home.
presence.hint_detail: When enabled, all rooms switch to eco temperature as soon as none of the configured persons are home. You can optionally restrict per room which persons are relevant.
presence.room_help_body: Select which persons are relevant for this room. The room switches to eco temperature when none of the selected persons are home. Without selection, the global rule applies: eco when nobody is home.
presence.room_none_assigned: Global rule — eco when nobody is home
presence.missing_entity_hint: This entity no longer exists in Home Assistant — uncheck it to remove it from this room.
presence.ignore_hint: Controls how this room reacts to presence. You can assign specific persons below. The room switches to eco when none of the assigned persons are home. Use the toggle above to skip detection entirely and always follow the schedule.
presence.help_ignore_body: When enabled, this room skips presence detection entirely. It always follows its schedule and never switches to eco based on who is home. Useful for rooms that should maintain temperature regardless of presence, such as a server room, a pet room, or a guest room used by someone not tracked by Home Assistant.
presence.tile_ignored: Presence detection is ignored. Room always follows its schedule.
presence.clears_override_hint: When nobody is home, manual overrides are paused and the room follows the away action. When someone returns, the override resumes until it expires.
valve_protection.title: Valve Protection
valve_protection.hint: Periodically opens idle TRV valves briefly to prevent seizing or calcification.
valve_protection.interval_hint: How long a valve can be idle before being cycled (1–90 days)
compressor.title: Compressor Protection
compressor.members_hint: Select all climate devices powered by this compressor (indoor splits, TRVs on radiators, fan coils).
compressor.min_run_hint: Compressor must run at least this long once started.
compressor.min_off_hint: Compressor must stay off at least this long after stopping.
compressor.master_entity_hint: The central unit that powers the indoor devices in this group, e.g. a gas boiler, outdoor heat pump unit, or ducted AC master switch. RoomMind will turn it on when any room needs heating or cooling, and off when all rooms are idle. Leave empty to use only the action script or short-cycle protection.
compressor.conflict_resolution_hint: Determines what happens when some rooms need heating while others need cooling at the same time. Heating priority: heating always wins (safest for frost protection). Cooling priority: cooling always wins. Majority: the mode with more rooms wins, ties go to heating. Outdoor temperature: uses the outdoor heating max threshold from settings to decide automatically.
compressor.action_script_hint: A Home Assistant script that runs whenever the heating/cooling demand changes. Useful for systems that need special commands, e.g. cancelling a Vaillant Quick Veto or toggling a relay. Works with or without a master device. Without a master device, only the script is triggered. Receives variables: action (heat/cool/idle), master_entity, members, active_members.
compressor.enforce_uniform_mode_hint: All thermostats in this group must operate in the same HVAC mode (all heating or all cooling). Rooms that disagree with the resolved group mode will be set to idle. Use this for heat pumps that start automatically but require all connected units to run the same mode.
mold.title: Mold Risk Protection
mold.detection_desc: Receive notifications when humidity indicates mold risk
mold.threshold_hint: Alert when room humidity stays above this value
mold.sustained_hint: Alert only after risk persists for this long
mold.prevention_desc: Dry at-risk walls with a dehumidifier or protected DRY cycles. Never heats; at night the AC only acts on a critical risk.
mold.prevention_sustained_hint: At 65% estimated wall RH, early DRY may start after 2 hours. At 70%, this duration applies; at 80%, at most 10 minutes. Cycles last up to 30 minutes with a 60-minute retry pause.
mold.dehumidification_desc: Use an AC's dry mode first only when the room is warm enough; otherwise RoomMind uses its configured heat-pump / boiler plan.
mold.dehumidification_min_temperature_hi: DRY starts at this room temperature and stops 1°C below (21°C minimum). Applies to AC DRY only: a dedicated dehumidifier runs at any temperature.

settings.intro.control: Choose how RoomMind controls your climate devices and set priority and thresholds.
settings.intro.presence: Automatically reduce temperature when nobody is home.
settings.intro.vacation: Set all rooms to a reduced temperature while you are away.
settings.intro.valve: Periodically move idle TRV valves to prevent seizing or calcification.
settings.intro.compressor: Manage groups of indoor units that share an outdoor compressor or central heating source. Optionally assign a master device (boiler, outdoor unit) to automatically turn on/off based on room demand. Short-cycle protection prevents rapid on/off switching that can damage equipment.
settings.intro.mold: Monitor humidity and automatically reduce mold risk.
settings.intro.notifications: Configure who receives alerts and how.
settings.intro.learning: Manage thermal model training and accelerate re-learning after changes.
settings.intro.reset: Clear learned thermal model data. The model will start learning from scratch.
notifications.title: Notifications
notifications.window_open_after_hint: Send an alert after this many minutes with the window open. Set 0 to disable.
notifications.enabled_hint: When disabled, no notifications are sent — neither to devices nor to the HA sidebar.
notifications.desc: Choose which devices receive alerts. Without targets, alerts appear in the HA sidebar.
notifications.add_target_hint: Type the entity ID if your device is not listed (e.g. notify.mobile_app_...). You can find it under Settings → Devices → your phone → Notify entity.
notifications.cooldown_hint: Minimum time between repeated alerts per room
notifications.mold_prevention_notify_hin: Also send a notification when prevention activates (temperature raised)
heat_source.power_estimate_hint: RoomMind automatically learns peak demand for heating, cooling and dry modes, adding 30% headroom. This backup is only used until each mode has at least 6 valid samples. With 0 W, starts without learned data are safely blocked.
preview.title: Safety preview
preview.intro: Read-only simulation of AC electrical budget and compressor admission.
preview.scope: Does not switch any device. Shows hypothetical start admission from current power readings; schedules, season gates and thermal MPC are not simulated.
preview.not_acknowledged: not confirmed (normal if boiler is off)
preview.reason_eligible: Eligible to start based on electrical/compressor safety
preview.reason_room_safety: Room safety gate (window or forced off)
heat_source.toggle_hint: When this room has both radiator thermostats and an AC/heat pump, RoomMind intelligently routes heating demand to the most efficient device based on temperature gap and outdoor conditions.
heat_source.primary_delta_hint: Only activate the primary source when the temperature gap exceeds this value. Below this threshold, only the fast secondary source is used.
heat_source.outdoor_threshold_hint: Above this outdoor temperature, prefer the AC/heat pump (higher efficiency). Below, prefer the gas boiler/radiator.
heat_source.ac_min_outdoor: Min. outdoor temp for AC heating
heat_source.ac_min_outdoor_hint: Disable AC heating entirely below this temperature to protect the heat pump hardware.
devices.keep_fan_only_window_hint: Heating and cooling pause, but an AC already in fan-only mode stays on.
settings.temperature_rounding_hint: When a climate device cannot represent RoomMind's 0.5° setpoint, choose how the physical target is rounded.
devices.power_sensor_hint: Instantaneous electrical consumption sensor for this AC. W and kW sensors are supported and used for energy history and adaptive predictions.
analytics.energy_subtitle: Measured device power and learned forecast
analytics.energy_chart_info_body: Solid lines show measured power. Dashed segments continue from the latest measurement with the learned three-hour forecast. Tap a legend item to hide or restore a series. Pinch or scroll horizontally to zoom; the vertical dashed line marks now.
analytics.comparison_info: Compare the selected period: kWh is measured climate energy, € is its estimated cost, Active is total heating/cooling time, ΔT/kWh shows temperature change per unit of energy, and To target is the average time to reach the scheduled temperature.

hero.power_budget_blocked: Climate start delayed by house power budget
hero.preconditioning_active: Pre-conditioning active for the next scheduled target
hero.ac_efficiency_issue: AC is using normal power but responding slowly

insights.comfort.title: Comfort score explained
insights.comfort.summary: Starts at 100; active conditions subtract points.
comfort.night_mode_hint: Gradually adjusts the room targets during the selected night period. Dehumidifiers run with the quiet fan and start only for mold prevention.
dehumidifier.title: Dehumidifier
dehumidifier.device_hint: Choose a dehumidifier or smart plug. Plug-controlled appliances must restart when power returns.
dehumidifier.manual_hint: RoomMind does not touch manual runs (e.g. laundry drying).
dehumidifier.forecast_estimate: default estimate, improves as the unit runs
dehumidifier.power_entity_hint: Real power draw in W or kW. Used instead of the nominal power for the forecast.
dehumidifier.forecast_unreachable: Target likely not reachable within 12 hours at this speed.
dehumidifier.host_included: The room hosting the device is always included.
dehumidifier.shared_hint: Shared control uses each room’s own sensor. Host window and night rules apply; pause at 45% and resume at 50% in the host, subject to device limits.
dehumidifier.power_hint: Required for new starts when the electrical power budget is enabled.
dehumidifier.comfort_hint: Adding a device does not enable comfort automatically. Active profiles can override this room’s humidity target. Mold prevention follows its existing settings.
dehumidifier.empty: No dedicated or shared device assigned. Automatic AC Dry remains available.
dehumidifier.tank_sensor_hint: Optional. When it reports full, RoomMind waits and does not treat the stop as a manual one.
dehumidifier.fan_entity_hint: Optional. While the dehumidifier runs, RoomMind sets the fan to "low" at night and "auto" by day, if the entity supports those options.
dehumidifier.user_off_hint: Automatic control resumes at {time} or when humidity is back on target.
dehumidifier.reason_power_budget: Waiting for electrical capacity or nominal power
dehumidifier.intro: Choose who controls the appliance, which rooms it serves, and the humidity goal for this room.
dehumidifier.guide_device: Automatic lets RoomMind start and stop the appliance for humidity comfort or mold prevention. Global climate control and climate control in the host room must both be enabled. Manual leaves control to you.
dehumidifier.guide_comfort: Each room opts into humidity comfort separately and has its own target. Mold prevention follows its own settings, even with comfort off. Active profiles can override the room target.
dehumidifier.guide_shared: Selecting a room lets its humidity demand request this appliance. Each served room needs a humidity reading. Air must circulate between rooms; the host’s windows, quiet hours and humidity protection apply to the whole appliance.
dehumidifier.disabled_hint: To allow automatic starts, enable climate control in general settings and in the host room, {room}. Enabling humidity comfort alone is not enough.
dehumidifier.auto_hint: RoomMind manages its own runs and supported humidity setpoints. If you turn the device on, it leaves it untouched until you turn it off.
dehumidifier.manual_option_hint: You control the appliance through Home Assistant.
dehumidifier.coverage_hint: Register the appliance where it is located. Add other rooms only if air can circulate between them.
dehumidifier.shared_available: A shared appliance already serves this room
dehumidifier.shared_available_hint: You can configure this room’s comfort below without adding another appliance. Change sharing in the host room.
dehumidifier.tolerance_hint: Tolerance and priority determine how far humidity can rise above the target before requesting drying. A larger margin reduces starts. Drying stops near the target.

air_quality.hint: With a CO₂ or VOC sensor RoomMind shows when the air gets stale and offers a binary sensor for automations. A ventilation unit (fan, switch) is switched on until the air is fresh again.
air_quality.voc_threshold_hint: In the sensor's own unit (index, ppb, µg/m³). Empty: the reading is shown but not judged.
air_quality.ventilation_hint: Switched on while the air is bad and off again once it is fresh (at least 15 minutes). RoomMind only switches off what it switched on.

schedule.residual_control_hint: Lets the radiators stop earlier when the heat they store (see Analytics, Learned Afterglow) carries the room to its target, and skips pre-heat runs the stored heat makes unnecessary. Off: heating ignores what was learned. Works once at least one run was learned.

devices.valve_closing_mode_info: TRVZB: the valve sits at X with opening X and closing 100 - X. TRV-ZBT: the second value is the opening while the TRV does not heat, both are set to X.

schedule.preheat_precool_hint: Turn off for rooms that should not warm up or cool down beforehand, e.g. a bedroom at night. Heating and cooling then start only shortly before the block.
schedule.preheat_precool_label: Pre-heat and pre-cool before schedule blocks
schedule.precool_hint: Turn off for rooms that should not cool down beforehand. Cooling then starts only shortly before the block.
schedule.follow_device_setpoint_label: Take over changes made on the device
schedule.follow_device_setpoint_hint: Only for devices that report their setpoint to Home Assistant. Leave it off if a device or an automation changes the setpoint by itself (own schedule, frost or window protection).
schedule.help_temps_adjust: On top of that: an empty room (occupancy sensors) keeps the schedule at eco at most, the electricity price can shift the schedule target, and mold protection raises the heat target.
schedule.eco_hint: Applies when the schedule is off, nobody is home or the room is empty, depending on your settings, and when you pick Eco.
devices.occupancy_eco: Eco when the room is empty
devices.setback_auto_off: Turn off after an hour without demand
devices.coil_dry_global_off_hint: Evaporator drying is off in the settings, so it does not run for this device. Turn it on there, or set this device to "Always on".
devices.info.intro: What each setting does is under the info icon next to it. How RoomMind drives thermostats and ACs is in the documentation.
covers.window_hold_hint: While a window or door sensor of this room reports open, RoomMind does not lower the covers and catches up once it is closed. For covers that would hit an open window (inside covers, roof windows). A cover that is already moving is not stopped.
settings.control_mode_hint: Predictive: RoomMind plans with the learned room model. While it is still learning, it simply switches on and off. Simple: always just on and off. The model keeps learning anyway, and the covers then use a simpler sun estimate.
settings.preheat_lead: Pre-heats or pre-cools up to {time} before a schedule block.
settings.preheat_lead_none: No pre-heating or pre-cooling: starts only shortly before a schedule block.
settings.preheat_lead_horizon: Pre-heats or pre-cools as early as the planning horizon reaches.
analytics.deviation_collecting: Still collecting: needs a few hours of data recorded since the update
analytics.afterglow_sub: In this room it fades in about {time}.
analytics.afterglow_unmeasured: Not measured yet: RoomMind measures it after the next heating runs.
analytics.info.now: Computed from the learned model for the current room and outdoor temperature and sun, at full power. RoomMind plans with exactly these figures: on a cold day heating takes longer and the room cools faster, so it starts earlier. The values change with the weather, the model keeps learning with every reading.
analytics.info.deviation: How far off the model was after one hour in the selected range. For every reading RoomMind runs the model one hour forward from the reading an hour before, with what really happened in between (heating or cooling, outdoor temperature, sun, open windows), and compares it with the reading. It uses today's model, so after a change to the room older days count against it. The smaller the value, the better RoomMind can time pre-heating and switching off. The dashed grey line in the chart shows the same hour by hour.
analytics.comfort_pending: Time on target appears once RoomMind has recorded targets for this room.
analytics.rhythm_hint: Click a date or a cell to show that day above, point at a cell to see the hour.
analytics.rhythm_hint_touch: Tap a date to show that day above, a cell to see the hour.
analytics.info.summary: On target means the room was at most {tolerance} below its heating target or above its cooling target. A room that only heats can only be too cold, one that only cools only too warm. Times with an open window do not count. Runs come from one reading every 3 to 5 minutes, so very short runs can be missing. After a heating run the room often keeps warming for a while: "then avg." is how far it went past the target the run heated for within the hour after it. A pre-heat run counts against the coming target (cooling likewise below the target).
analytics.info.heat_loss: How fast the room cools down without heating at the difference to outside shown above (twice that difference means twice as fast). The lower, the better insulated. To judge a renovation, compare the value before and after. Learned from the room's own behavior; per hour rather than in watts because the model does not know the size of the room.
analytics.info.afterglow: How much warmer a 10-minute heating run still makes the room after it stops, because the radiators have stored heat, and how long that takes to fade. RoomMind measures this after every run and stops heating earlier to match. If it is large, the room heats in shorter steps so it does not overshoot.
settings.orphans_delete_confirm: Delete "{name}" with its settings and learned data?
settings.reset_room_confirm_history: Delete the history of this outdoor area?
settings.reset_room_confirm_no_model: Delete this room's history? Without a temperature sensor or device it learns no model.
settings.boost_confirm: New measurements count more until the next heating or cooling runs are measured. This cannot be undone.
learning.boost_info: After "Re-learn faster" new measurements count more for a while, so the model picks up a change in the room sooner. It fades by itself. The time left is an estimate, it only runs while the room learns (window closed, outdoor temperature known).
presence.room_none_assigned_off: Everyone counts: devices off when nobody is home
presence.room_disabled: Presence is off in the settings. What you set here only takes effect once it is on there.
presence.room_no_persons: No person is set up in the settings yet. Until then no room goes to eco or off because nobody is home.
presence.ignore_info: The room never goes to eco or off because nobody is home. For example a guest room or a room that should always stay warm.
presence.persons_info: When none of these people is home, the away rule applies to the room (eco or off). Without a choice everyone from the settings counts.
compressor.draft_no_members: Saved once it has an indoor unit.
coil_dry.title: Evaporator drying
coil_dry.hint: Applies to every AC unless set otherwise on the device.
coil_dry.duration_hint: How long the fan keeps running (1–60 min). At a low fan speed about twice as long as at a high one.
coil_dry.min_cooling_hint: Only dry once the AC has cooled this long. Short cooling runs are added up (1–240 min).
coil_dry.mode_dry_warning: When dehumidifying the compressor keeps running and cools the fins down again, which works against drying. Only pick this if your device's dry mode mainly runs the fan.
coil_dry.fan_mode_hint: Higher dries faster but is louder. If the device does not know the speed, it keeps its current one.
coil_dry.drain_hint: The AC stays off first so the condensate can drain, then the fan starts (0–15 min). Less moisture is blown back into the room.
mold.insulation_hint: Used to estimate how cold the coldest spot of your exterior walls gets (corners, window reveals). Well insulated means new or renovated. If unsure, keep Standard. Needs an outdoor temperature.
mold.intensity_hint: Warmer air makes cold spots on the wall drier. The stronger, the more heating energy. Light is usually enough.
notifications.mold_off: Mold detection is off, so RoomMind reports nothing.
notifications.mold_off_prevention: Mold detection is off. Messages only come when RoomMind heats to prevent mold.
notifications.target_person_missing: Without a person the message is always sent.
heat_source.rule_gap: Radiators from {delta} below target, else AC
heat_source.both_from: Both heat from {delta} below the target
heat_source.help_body: Only in rooms with a room sensor, a thermostat and an AC, and only while heating. With an outdoor temperature it alone decides: above the switch point the AC heats, below it the radiators. Without one, the radiators heat from the set gap to the target, the AC below it. From twice the gap plus 0.3 K both heat until the gap drops below the set value. Below the minimum outdoor temperature the AC never heats. With the price option, expensive power means radiators and cheap power the AC; at a normal price the rules above apply.
devices.type_info: Thermostat for radiator valves and underfloor heating, AC for anything that cools or heats with air. This decides how RoomMind drives the device.
devices.managed_note: Without a room sensor every device regulates with its own sensor. Setpoint mode and valve control need a temperature sensor in the room.
devices.setpoint_mode_info: Proportional: RoomMind moves the device's setpoint and so controls how hard it heats or cools. Direct: the device gets the room's target temperature and regulates on its own.
devices.setpoint_offset_info: Added to the room target before it goes to the device. If the device reads 2 degrees colder than your room sensor, enter -2.
devices.idle_info_trv: What the thermostat gets when the room needs no heat. "Low setpoint" keeps it at its minimum instead of off, for wireless thermostats that fall asleep when off and then miss commands.
devices.idle_info_ac: "Turn off" switches the device off. "Fan only" keeps the fan running. "Setback" leaves it on and moves the setpoint {delta} away from the room target, e.g. for multi-split systems.
devices.idle_fan_mode_info: Fan speed while the idle device only runs its fan.
devices.setback_auto_off_info: Switches the device off when it had nothing to do for an hour and RoomMind does not need it in the next hour either. Only works once the room model has learned and controls predictively.
devices.valve_opening_info: The number entity Home Assistant uses to set the valve opening, e.g. valve_opening_degree. Leave it empty to hand the valve back to the thermostat.
devices.valve_closing_info: The number entity for the closing degree, e.g. valve_closing_degree. It holds the valve at the set opening, whatever the thermostat wants. Filled in when it is named like the opening.
devices.valve_idle_opening_info: The valve opening while the thermostat is not heating, e.g. idle_valve_position in Zigbee2MQTT.
devices.valve_protection_exclude_info: Valve protection then leaves this valve alone. Useful for entities without a real valve, e.g. a virtual boiler.
devices.coil_dry_info: After cooling the fan keeps running for a while without cooling, so the evaporator dries and does not smell musty. "As global" follows Settings › Evaporator drying.
devices.coil_dry_minutes_info: How long the device runs its fan after cooling.
devices.coil_dry_mode_info: "Fan only" almost always fits. Pick "Dehumidify" only if the device's dry mode mainly runs the fan, else the compressor cools the fins down again.
devices.coil_dry_fan_mode_info: Fan speed while drying. "Keep current speed" leaves the fan as it is.
devices.heating_system_type_scope: Applies to all thermostats in this room.

settings.intro.price: Rooms heat and cool a little more while electricity is cheap and a little less while it is expensive.
settings.price_entity_hint: A price sensor (Tibber, Nordpool, EPEX Spot, aWATTar, ENTSO-e, Octopus, template) or a switch that is on while power is cheap (PV surplus, off-peak tariff). If the sensor has a forecast (raw_today/raw_tomorrow, data, prices, …), RoomMind heats ahead of expensive hours, otherwise it compares the price with the last days. The unit does not matter.
settings.price_unreadable: The price source has no usable value right now. Rooms keep their schedule until it does.
settings.price_kind_history: no forecast, ranked against the last {hours} h
settings.price_kind_history_learning: no forecast, collecting prices ({hours} of {needed} h)
schedule.price_shift_hint: When electricity is cheap the target may rise a little, when it is expensive it may drop a little (cooling the other way round). This only helps if the room heats or cools with electricity (heat pump, AC, electric heater); with a gas or oil boiler it does nothing.
heat_source.price_aware_hint: Only useful when the radiators run on gas, oil or district heat: expensive power, the radiators heat; cheap power, the AC. On a cold day (below “AC above outdoor”) the AC then only takes gaps smaller than “Gap to target”; a larger one, such as heating up for the next comfort period, stays with the radiators. At a normal price the outdoor rule still decides. Far below the target both heat.
analytics.price_shifted: Target moved by the price for {value}
hero.price_charging: Electricity cheap: target {value} to store heat
hero.setback_info: The room needs no heating or cooling right now. Devices with the idle action "Setback" stay on in their mode with a lowered setpoint, so they can pick up again quickly. With "Turn off after an hour without demand" they switch off once the hour is over and RoomMind does not need them in the next hour either.

sensors.temp_info: With a sensor RoomMind measures the room itself and tells the devices when to heat or cool (Full Control). Without one the devices regulate with their own sensor (Managed).
sensors.full_control_note: Full Control: RoomMind regulates by this sensor. Without it the devices regulate on their own again.
sensors.device_sensor_note: RoomMind controls by the device's own sensor. It sits next to the radiator or at the air inlet and often reads warmer or colder than the room. A separate room sensor controls more precisely.
sensors.outdoor_note: Only measured and shown, nothing is controlled.
sensors.humidity_info: Shows the humidity and is needed for the mold warning. Without a sensor the room gets no mold warning.
sensors.window_info: While a window or door is open, RoomMind pauses heating and cooling in this room.
sensors.window_open_delay_info: How long a window has to be open before RoomMind pauses. A short opening then interrupts nothing.
sensors.window_close_delay_info: How long RoomMind waits after closing before it heats or cools again.
sensors.occupancy_info: Motion or presence sensors in the room. RoomMind uses them to learn how much heat people add and can switch an empty room to eco.
sensors.occupancy_eco_info: When all sensors report the room empty for longer than the delay, eco applies until someone is back. The room then only warms up once someone is in it. A temporary temperature, vacation and presence come first.
sensors.occupancy_eco_delay_info: How long all sensors have to report nothing before eco applies (5 to 240 minutes).
sensors.help: RoomMind suggests the sensors of the room's area. The search under each group also takes a sensor from another area. What a sensor does is explained at the group's info icon.

settings.summary.notify_no_source: On, but mold detection is off
sensors.co2_info: A CO₂ sensor (ppm) tells when the air is stale. RoomMind then shows a hint, switches a binary sensor for your own automations and can switch a ventilation unit on.
sensors.voc_info: A VOC sensor reacts to cooking, cleaning agents and off-gassing. It works like the CO₂ sensor once you set a threshold in the sensor's unit.
sensors.ventilation_info: A fan, switch or input_boolean that ventilates the room, e.g. an extractor fan or the boost of a ventilation system with heat recovery. Recirculating air (an AC's fan mode) does not lower the CO₂.
sensors.ventilation_note: RoomMind switches it on when the air turns bad and off again once it is good, after at least 15 minutes. It only switches off what it switched on itself. With climate control off it switches nothing on, and one it runs goes off.
sensors.no_ventilation: None. Without one, RoomMind only shows the air quality.
sensors.co2_threshold_info: From this value on the air counts as stale, good again below 80 % of it (below 800 ppm at 1000). The German Environment Agency rates below 1000 ppm as harmless and asks for more fresh air from 1000 ppm on.
sensors.voc_threshold_info: In the sensor's unit. VOC sensors report an index, ppb or µg/m³, so there is no default. For a µg/m³ sensor the German Environment Agency rates TVOC above 1000 µg/m³ as conspicuous; index sensors (100 = the room's daily average) often use 250. Good again below 80 % of the threshold. Empty the field to only show the value.
sensors.voc_not_judged: No threshold: the value is only shown.
card.hint.air_bad: Poor air quality, air the room
schedules.note: Schedules are Home Assistant schedule helpers and not tied to a room: every room can use any of them, for its temperature (room › Schedule & temperatures) or its covers (room › Covers & blinds).
schedule_editor.cover_block_legend: Force position: the covers move to the block's position (0 % = closed). Allow solar protection: RoomMind may shade during the block.
schedule_editor.cover_no_block_legend: RoomMind runs the covers itself; with “Allow solar protection” it does not shade.
schedule_editor.mixed_notice: {climate} uses this schedule for the temperature, {cover} for the covers. Every block therefore also gets a position; without one it counts as closed.
schedule_editor.delete_effect_cover_none: In {rooms} the covers then run without a schedule.
schedule_editor.delete_selector_last_cov: If the switch in {rooms} points to this schedule, the covers there run without a schedule afterwards.
schedule_editor.cover_position_hint: 0 % = closed, 100 % = open. Applies where a room uses the schedule with “Force position”.
schedule_editor.cover_position_gate: The rooms use this schedule only to allow solar protection: the position does not count there.
